Official written history says the foundations were completed in spring 1827, construction stopped that June, and substantial construction resumed only in 1834. Portray that LOW FOUNDATION/BASEMENT stage, not a standing palace. This is an approximate fictional site arrangement, not a reproduction of any Linstow drawing, museum collection picture, existing artwork or exact construction plan.
Main subject: a LONG LOW pale stone masonry foundation and unfinished basement wall courses on the left half of the hilltop, only about waist-high or at most one metre high above the surrounding soil. Individual unfinished masonry courses and open foundation trenches are clear, but there is NO finished above-ground facade, no multi-storey building, no roof or roof beams, no windows, no columns, no portico, no temple pediment and no completed projecting wings. Uneven temporary rough timber scaffolding with plain planks and slender braced uprights stands only beside the low masonry. Foundation is completely visible inside the image with ample margins.
Construction materials and tools: modest piles of rough pale stone and a few neatly stacked cut blocks near the foundation, one simple wooden handcart, a small wooden tripod with a rope pulley and hand windlass for lifting stone, lowered idle ropes. Two plain wooden-handled masonry tools resting on the soil in the foreground, quiet and unused. All tools, scaffolds and materials are plausible for Norwegian building work in the 1820s; no industrial machinery. No people are necessary, and prefer NO people at all.
Composition: distant wide view from the foot of the gently rising bare grassy hill, at ordinary human eye level looking uphill. The long low masonry foundation sits LEFT of centre in the middle distance. The foreground and right half are mostly empty rough earth and worn grass, with idle tools, shallow wheel ruts and scattered small stones. Sparse distant autumn trees, a gray overcast autumn sky and no visible surrounding buildings. Enough close ground texture to read as a real camera photograph while keeping the whole low foundation legible.
Medium and lighting: highly convincing camera-shot photograph-like historical reconstruction with natural soft muted gray autumn daylight, restrained pale stone, weathered wood, earth brown and dull grass colors. Normal documentary wide-lens perspective and exposure, physically natural textures. Calm quiet empty-site mood. No dramatic fog or fantasy atmosphere. No HDR, no cinematic grading, no oversaturated colors, no painterly look, no CGI sheen.
Avoid: standing palace or substantial above-ground facade, modern Royal Palace front or rear, completed wings, columns, portico, pediment, roof, tall walls, ornate finished plaster, modern buildings, cars, asphalt, power lines, modern cranes, mechanical vehicles, site boards, readable words/numbers, signs, flags, emblems, logos, captions, watermarks, frames, identifiable human faces or actual persons, copied historical plans/drawings or protected museum collection art.
